title: Shipping a Faster Next.js App: 7 Changes That Mattered
excerpt: A practical checklist of Next.js changes that improve Core Web Vitals.
metaTitle: Shipping a Faster Next.js App: 7 Changes That Mattered
metaDescription: A practical checklist of Next.js changes that improve Core Web Vitals.
featuredImageAlt: Shipping a Faster Next.js App: 7 Changes That Mattered
body:
Performance work is mostly about measuring before you guess. Here are seven changes that usually make the biggest difference.

## 1. Move data fetching to the server
Server Components let you fetch on the server and ship zero client JavaScript for static sections.

```tsx
export default async function Page() {
  const posts = await getPosts();
  return <PostList posts={posts} />;
}
```

## 2. Use `next/image` everywhere
Automatic AVIF/WebP and correct `sizes` cut image bytes by more than half.

## 3. Cache aggressively, revalidate deliberately
Tag your fetches and call `revalidateTag` from mutations instead of disabling caching.

## 4. Lazy-load heavy client widgets
Charts and editors can load with `dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr: false })`.

## 5. Audit your fonts
Self-host with `next/font` and subset to the glyphs you use.

## 6. Kill layout shift
Reserve space for images and embeds.

## 7. Watch the bundle
Run the bundle analyzer on every major dependency bump.

## Wrapping up
None of these are exotic; the win comes from doing all of them consistently.

title: From Side Project to Portfolio Piece
excerpt: How to present a side project so it tells a story recruiters and clients remember.
metaTitle: From Side Project to Portfolio Piece
metaDescription: How to present a side project so it tells a story recruiters and clients remember.
featuredImageAlt: From Side Project to Portfolio Piece
body:
A good portfolio entry answers three questions fast: what is it, why does it matter, and what did you do.

## Lead with the outcome
"Cut checkout time in half" beats "Built a checkout page".

## Show, don't tell
A short video or three good screenshots do more than paragraphs of text.

## Explain one hard decision
Pick a single trade-off and explain why you chose it.

## Keep it current
Archive projects that no longer represent your best work. Fewer, stronger entries win.

title: Designing Accessible Forms Without Losing Your Mind
excerpt: Practical patterns for labels, errors and focus management that work for everyone.
metaTitle: Designing Accessible Forms Without Losing Your Mind
metaDescription: Practical patterns for labels, errors and focus management that work for everyone.
featuredImageAlt: Designing Accessible Forms Without Losing Your Mind
body:
Forms are where accessibility issues hurt users the most. A few habits fix most of them.

## Always use real labels
Placeholders are not labels. Pair every input with a `<label htmlFor>`.

## Announce errors
Link error text with `aria-describedby` and move focus to the first invalid field on submit.

## Keep the tab order natural
If you need `tabIndex` greater than 0, the layout is probably wrong.

## Test with a keyboard and a screen reader
Five minutes with VoiceOver or NVDA catches more than any linter.

## Checklist
- Visible focus styles
- Sufficient color contrast
- Clear, specific error messages

title: Postgres Tips Every Full Stack Developer Should Know
excerpt: Indexes, EXPLAIN, and a few features that save you from writing extra code.
metaTitle: Postgres Tips Every Full Stack Developer Should Know
metaDescription: Indexes, EXPLAIN, and a few features that save you from writing extra code.
featuredImageAlt: Postgres Tips Every Full Stack Developer Should Know
body:
You don't need to be a DBA to get a lot out of Postgres.

## Read the query plan
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` tells you what actually happened, not what you hoped would happen.

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;
```

## Index what you filter and sort by
Composite indexes follow the left-most rule; order the columns accordingly.

## Use partial indexes
Index only the rows you query, like `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.

## Let the database enforce rules
Constraints and unique indexes beat application-level checks every time.

## JSONB is a tool, not a schema
Great for flexible metadata; keep core relations in real columns.
